---
title: Trigram index — implementation plan
kind: plan
---

## Goal

Land the on-disk trigram index behind the existing `helio search` surface, so a
query over a 1 GB corpus returns its first hit in under 200 ms without changing
a single CLI flag.

### Where the time goes today

<Table
  id="latency"
  columns={["Corpus", "v1 scan", "trigram (spike)", "First hit"]}
  rows={[
    ["120 MB", "1.4 s", "0.09 s", "streamed"],
    ["500 MB", "11.2 s", "0.14 s", "streamed"],
    ["2.3 GB", "58.0 s", "0.18 s", "streamed"]
  ]}
/>

### The shape of the change

<Diff
  id="writer"
  filename="helio/search/writer.rs"
  language="rust"
  mode="split"
  before={"let mut candidates = Vec::new();\nfor hit in scan(corpus) {\n    candidates.push(hit.range());\n}\ndedup(&mut candidates);\n"}
  after={"let mut candidates = BoundedSet::new(cap);\nfor hit in index.probe(query) {\n    candidates.insert(hit.range());\n}\n"}
  annotations={[
    { lines: "1", note: "Bounded up front — the unbounded Vec is what the OOM incident hit." },
    { lines: "2-4", note: "Probe the index instead of scanning; dedup is incremental." }
  ]}
/>

<Callout id="decision" tone="decision">

**Chosen: memory-mapped postings with a 64 MB sliding window.** A fully
in-memory index was 3× faster on the spike but needs the whole corpus resident,
which is exactly the failure mode reported in
[[search-crash-large-logs]]. The sliding window keeps the resident set flat and
costs ~20 ms on the 2.3 GB corpus.

</Callout>
